provenance.method: Technology/sensory question using built-in platform settings as descriptive options rather than treatment claims.

question: My device is visually busy or distracting. What built-in settings can reduce motion, interruptions or cognitive load?
why_it_matters: Animation, notifications, clutter and competing prompts can make a device harder to use even when the underlying task is simple.
current_understanding: Inspect settings for reduced motion or animation, notification control, focus modes, simplified reading and display options. Change one variable at a time so the effect is visible. These settings are accommodations, not treatment for ADHD, autism or another condition.
evidence_needed: Independent evidence on distraction-reduction and reduced-motion features for neurodivergent users.
Cross-platform setup guides that stay current without collecting user data.
reopening_conditions: Major platform updates change these controls.
Stronger usability evidence supports specific default configurations.
dissent: Aggressively suppressing notifications can cause missed obligations; the useful balance depends on what information is actually time-sensitive.
